title: I've been making my first game with AI tools since August. This is one of its 45 bosses.
author: Affectionate_Bend402
selftext:
Hi everyone! I'm making One More Room, a roguelite auto-battler. You place up to 5 heroes, they fight on their own, and you decide when to stop going deeper. If your party dies, you lose everything you carried.



Almost everything in it was made with AI:

\- Code: mostly Claude Code, in Godot

\- 3D models and animations: Meshy

\- Music, most sound effects and the narrator: ElevenLabs

\- Concept art and icons: gpt-image-2, Nano Banana and a few others



I direct, I playtest, and I decide what stays.



The last big step was the bosses. Meshy's auto-rig made their weapons bend like noodles, and it took a Blender script to fix that. Now all 45 have their own model and moves.



The game is on Steam as Coming Soon. Before Early Access I'm looking for a few playtesters, because I don't want to launch with a lot of bugs. Links are in the comments.



English is not my first language, so sorry for any mistakes. Happy to answer questions about the workflow!

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: How long did it take you? I feel like I'm progressing really slow even though I have a similar style as yours, I'm using Tripo but I'm not delegating enough or implementing scripts idk

replies.author: Affectionate_Bend402
replies.body:
Thanks for asking! I started in late August, so about 2 and a half months so far.

For going faster, what worked for me is to take a lot of time on the first one. Pick your first boss (or first monster) and get everything working on it: the scripts, the import, the Blender fixes. Then teach your AI that exact process and let it reuse the same scripts, including how to patch the model in Blender.

That way, when you decide to make more bosses later, the AI already knows how to do it, so you mostly just implement them. For each new boss you only ask for the parts that are different, depending on the style you're going for.

What are you making? I'd like to see it!
